Use the saved findings below to revise the approach. Preserve unresolved obligations as open work; treat model notes as unverified.

Saved findings and criticism:
Artifact 1: Revisit the six-state transfer strategy using the earlier counterexample and later independent encoding: exact DP through n=60 agrees with the candidate order-12, step-three recurrence, but this finite check does not establish it for all n.
Skeptic objections: Finite recurrence residuals through n=48 are corroboration, not a proof for arbitrary n. · The transfer matrices are periodic but do not commute in general; the three-step product order must be stated and verified. · Even a proved recurrence and a_12 value would not by itself establish the requested limiting ratio without control of characteristic roots and coefficients.
Open obligations: Derive the order-12 recurrence from exact phase-ordered transfer-matrix products for every n. · Verify all initial/boundary indices algebraically rather than only by DP. · Prove the nontrivial root-of-unity terms are negligible compared with F_(n+2). · Compute the exact three-step matrix product for each phase and show it yields the claimed recurrence. · State enough initial values and check the n=0 boundary exactly. · Prove the asymptotic contribution of the two nontrivial residue modes is o(F_(n+2)).
Coordinator decision: stop_budget_exhausted
Next question: None recorded

Parent approach follows:
Use a dynamic-programming state (r,b), with r in {0,1,2} the sum of selected indices modulo 3 and b indicating whether the most recently processed index was selected. On processing i, either omit i, which resets b=0, or include i only if b=0, updating r to r+i mod 3. Encode this as a 6-by-6 transition matrix T_i. Because T_{i+3}=T_i, calculate the three-step matrix and seek a polynomial identity satisfied by each residue-class subsequence of a_n. First tests: independently enumerate admissible subsets for n=0,...,8 and compare all three residues. Proof obligations: derive an exact constant-coefficient recurrence, list sufficient initial values, and bound nontrivial residue modes strongly enough to prove asymptotic equidistribution. If the matrix characteristic polynomial is unnecessarily large, look for invariant subspaces or symmetry reduction; do not infer a recurrence solely from samples.
